subject: Venue tiebreaker and expedited relief protocol (MSA redlines)
body:
--- Message 1 (original) ---
From: Ava Moreno <ava.moreno@edensystems.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: MSA redlines — governing law & injunctive carve (Eden)

Jordan — thanks for the call this morning.

Eden reviewed Redwood's MSA redlines and our legal team pushed back on two points: governing law and the injunctive-relief carve. High level: we prefer California law (home state) and want express forum selection in CA for temporary/emergency relief (we often need local county courts for expedited seizure/asset preservation).

Quick bullets:
- Governing law: CA (we understand Redwood's Delaware preference; open to compromise language)
- Injunctive relief: Eden requests that parties may seek provisional/interim measures in California courts with expedited procedures retained
- Arbitration: Eden accepts arbitration for merits but wants the emergency-relief carve preserved outside arbitration

Attached is our annotated MSA redline (Eden_MSA_redlines_20261111.pdf). Can Redwood propose narrow language that: (a) preserves arbitration for merits; (b) explicitly allows provisional remedies in CA courts without waiving arbitration; and (c) includes a tie-breaker if we still can't agree on seat/governing law?

I can loop in our procurement lead Samir if needed. Want to resolve before we finalize the order form.

Thanks,
Ava
Ava Moreno
Head of Legal Ops, Eden Systems
Ava.moreno@edensystems.com

--- Message 2 (reply) ---
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ava Moreno <ava.moreno@edensystems.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — governing law & injunctive carve (Eden)

Ava — appreciate the clear note and the redline. We want to get this wrapped this week so the pilot order can proceed.

High-level compromise proposal (we've validated with product/ops):
1) Governing law: Delaware law (consistent with our standard MSA) but include a narrow public-policy carve so that parties may seek provisional remedies in local courts necessary to preserve status quo or property.
2) Emergency relief: Either party may seek provisional/interim injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction (including California courts) without waiving the agreement to arbitrate merits. The arbitration clause will continue to govern substantive claims, with an express tolling/transfer mechanic if an order is issued by a court.
3) Tie-breaker protocol: if parties cannot agree on seat within 10 business days, the following hierarchy will apply: (a) seat where defendant is incorporated; (b) seat where majority of defendant's operations relevant to the contract are located; (c) if still unresolved, default to Delaware for governing law and seat for arbitration while preserving local-court access for provisional measures.

I've attached our suggested redline snippet in the attached Annotated_order_form_eden_20261112.docx for your review. The language is intentionally narrow — we want to preserve a single forum for the merits but keep safe path for emergency relief.

Proposed next step: if Eden is comfortable with the tie-breaker + explicit provisional-measures carve, we can push final MSA + order form to DocuSign today and include the arbitration onboarding steps in the order form.

Jordan Blake
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

--- Message 3 (internal legal / more detailed) ---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — governing law & injunctive carve (Eden)

Folks — quick legal note to tighten Jordan's draft before we send back.

Suggested clarifications to avoid broad waiver risk:
- Replace "may seek" with "may seek only provisional or interim injunctive relief" to make clear requests to courts are limited and do not address merits.
- Add explicit "no-waiver" sentence: "Pursuit of provisional remedies in court shall not be deemed a waiver of the parties' agreement to arbitrate the merits of any dispute."
- Service/notice: require 48-hour notice to the other party (by email + hub ID) before seeking provisional relief except where ex parte relief is permitted by the court.
- Emergency enforcement: carve limited to preservation of goodwill/assets/data—list examples (preserve KV caches, prevent account takeover, disable access) to reduce ambiguity.

I also recommend we avoid dual governing law; keep Delaware for uniformity (our Ops team prefers), but allow Eden a narrow enforcement window in CA courts for provisional steps. If Eden insists on CA law for the entire MSA, we should ask commercial for revenue concessions.

Attaching annotated order form with inline language.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
Attachment: Annotated_order_form_eden_20261112.docx

--- Message 4 (external) ---
From: Ava Moreno <ava.moreno@edensystems.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@eden-sys.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — governing law & injunctive carve (Eden)

Jordan/Kim — thanks for the quick turn. We can accept the narrow compromise with the following small tweaks:
- Confirmed: Eden accepts Delaware governing law for merits if we keep express, unqualified right to seek provisional remedies in California courts for expedited enforcement (we can't operationally accept delay).
- Notice: we are fine with the 48-hour notice carve but request a shorter 24-hour window for expedited matters where local statutes permit (courts may require quick action).
- Tie-breaker: acceptable as drafted.

If you can incorporate Kim's no-waiver sentence and update the notice window to 24 hours (with carve for ex parte), Eden will sign. I'll have procurement (Samir) push DocuSign once we receive the final redline.

I'll attach a short sign-off checklist and will expect a DocuSign link in the hour once redlines are in. Appreciate the flexibility here.

Best,
Ava
Ava Moreno
Head of Legal Ops, Eden Systems

--- End of thread ---
